newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran, India and Turkmenistan sign transit accord.
newsitem.headline: Iran, India and Turkmenistan sign transit accord.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Iran, Turkmenistan and India signed a trilateral transit agreement on Saturday in Tehran to facilitate cargo traffic among the three countries.

"Based on this agreement the three countries will cooperate in the area of cargo transportation and will provide each other with required facilities," Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said at a news conference in Tehran.
Velayati said the three ministers also agreed to accomodate Kazakhstan at a later stage as a fourth member in the transit accord.

He said the three countries were working on other important agreements for commercial and economic cooperation including a joint textile mill in Iran, a petrochemical complex, a store chain and a shipyard on the Caspian sea at the borders between Iran and Turkmenistan.
Indian External Affairs Minister I.K. Gujral said at the news conference that the trilateral accord was "a good manifestation of south-south cooperation."
Gujral said the accord "spells out the future of Asia."
Asked about U.S. sanctions against Iran, Gojral said India believes "no country has the right to unilaterally pose sanctions against another country."
"India has never been a party to that (U.S. sanctions)...we value our economic, cultural and political relations with Iran," he added.

Washington last summer approved sanctions to penalise non-American firms that invest $40 million or more in Iran's oil and gas sectors. The Unuetd States has branded Tehran as a leading supporter of international terrorism, among other things. Tehran denies the charges.

Iran, which lies between the remote deserts and steppes of Central Asia and the Gulf, is pushing its geographical position hard to strengthen its ties with its former Soviet neighbours to become the gateway for the landlocked Central Asian republics.
